key_insight: Twisting multilayer MoS2 breaks symmetry and reshapes electronic wavefunctions, activating new shift-current channels and making the nonlinear photovoltaic response tunable by angle.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design knob for optimizing next-generation 2D photovoltaic and AI-enabled solar materials by engineering twist angle and layer stacking to enhance photocurrent generation.
method: Built a Slater-Koster tight-binding model for large moiré supercells, parametrized from first-principles calculations.
Compared tight-binding predictions against density functional theory and Wannier-interpolated results.
Analyzed shift-current conductivity and shift distance across mono-, bi-, trilayer, and twisted bilayer/trilayer structures.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces band-edge electronic structure and captures the main spectral features of shift-current conductivity, matching DFT and Wannier-based benchmarks.
watch_item: Large moiré systems still rely on parametrization and may miss effects beyond the fitted band-edge physics or idealized twist/disorder conditions.
paper_title: Twistronic control of shift current in multilayer moiré system
